answer: A sybil defense that works is sequential, non-parallelizable work per identity: every new agent must finish a verifiable delay computation that takes minutes of wall-clock time and cannot be sped up by adding machines. A crystal-clear rule follows: one identity costs one delay, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand sequential waits, while the honest newcomer pays the nectar-sweet price of a single short wait. Combined with a non-refundable fee per identity, the falcon-sharp cost scales linearly with every fake, while rewards stay capped, so farming identities turns unprofitable fast.
